assignment.acceptance_condition: Proved explicit lower bound N(H) >= c*log H from the chain with correct closed form AND the proved super-log bound N(H) >= c'(log H)^{log_3 2} (or a precisely identified obstruction with the chain bound kept); all family members proved solutions and proved distinct; under 600 words.
assignment.objective: D5: Prove the strongest rigorous lower bound for N(H). HARD CAP 600 words, terse lemma-proof. SKELETON: (L-A, chain) Define c_0=d_0? No: v_j=(1,1,c_j,d_j) with (c_1,d_1)=(1,3), c_{j+1}=d_j, d_{j+1}=4d_j-c_j. Prove by induction via the Vieta root-swap (state once: if (1,1,c,d) is a solution, mutating c gives solution (1,1,d,4d-c)) that every v_j is a solution, d_j strictly increasing, d_j = ((2+sqrt3)^j + (2-sqrt3)^j... derive the exact closed form: d_j solves x_{j+1}=4x_j-x_{j-1}? Verify: d_{j+1}=4d_j-c_j=4d_j-d_{j-1}, characteristic roots 2±sqrt3). Conclude N(H) >= log_{2+sqrt3}(H) - O(1): an explicit c*log H lower bound with c=1/ln(2+sqrt3). (L-B, binary subtree, the upgrade) At chain vertex v_j (j>=2), child u_j=(1,c_j,d_j,4c_jd_j-1) has max m_j<=4 d_j^2 and (prove) its two children-by-mutating-the-1-and-c_j are distinct; better: prove every off-chain vertex has at least 2 distinct children (mutations at a and at b; if a<b they differ since 4bcd-a vs 4acd-b: show inequality in one line; if a=b they coincide — handle). Then the binary tree rooted at u_j: at depth t the max is <= m_j^{3^t} * 4^{(3^t-1)/2} (from max' <= 4 max^3 induction) >= ... take logs: log max <= 3^t (log m_j + log 2). So depth-t binary subtree stays under H when 3^t (log m_j+log 2) <= log H, i.e. t >= log_3( log H / (log m_j + log 2) ). Total vertices from this subtree >= 2^t. Optimize over j (smallest m_j gives deepest t): with m_2 = 4*3*11-1=131: t = floor(log_3(log H / log 262...)) giving N(H) >= 2^{log_3(log H) - O(1)} = (log H)^{log 2/log 3 - o(1)}. Compute honestly and state the exact proved bound with explicit constants: N(H) >= max( log_{2+sqrt3} H - O(1), c' (log H)^{log_3 2} ) where log_3 2 approx 0.631, specifying for which H each dominates. If the binary-subtree distinctness step fails, prove it or drop to the chain bound and say exactly why. No tables, at most 2 one-line substitution checks.

context.task: Investigate the mutation graph of sorted positive-integer solutions of a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2 = 4abcd under Vieta mutation. First prove or refute the structural claims — connectivity of every solution to (1,1,1,1), uniqueness of a height-decreasing mutation at every non-root vertex, and the consequent rooted-tree structure of the quotient graph — then pursue the open asymptotic part: strongest attainable rigorous upper and lower bounds for N(H), the relation between mutation depth and log H, an active search for exceptional small solutions, hidden cycles, multiple parents, and induction failure modes, and sharply separated conjectures. Deliver a self-contained research memorandum.
